quotes: We have stratified 81 patients according to their patterns of disease manifestations and identified the HLA-DRB1 alleles by polymerase chain reaction amplification and subsequent oligonucleotide hybridization.

Rheumatoid nodules were highly associated with a heterozygosity for two disease associated HLA-DRB1 alleles. Homozygosity for the HLA-DRB1*0401 allele was a characteristic finding for RA patients with major organ involvement.

notes.statement: In an expression QTL study of purified CD4+ T cells and CD14+CD16- monocytes from 461 healthy individuals of European, African, and East Asian ancestry, Raj et al. (2014) found that rheumatoid arthritis susceptibility alleles, like those for multiple sclerosis and type 1 diabetes, showed a preponderance of T cell-specific cis-regulatory effects. In contrast, Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease alleles were enriched for monocyte-specific effects.
quotes: variants associated with some diseases display a preponderance of T cell–specific cis-regulatory effects: These include susceptibility alleles for multiple sclerosis, rheumatoid arthritis, and type 1 diabetes (Fig. 3, A and B).

Four diseases with significant polarization (FDR < 0.05) in the distribution of cis-eQTLs: Multiple sclerosis and rheumatoid arthritis are enriched in T cell effects (green), whereas Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s diseases are enriched in monocyte effects (orange).

notes.statement: Raj et al. (2014) found significant enrichment of cis-eQTLs among autoimmune disease-associated variants. Of 425 GWAS SNPs associated with one or more autoimmune diseases, 143 had cis-regulatory effects on 164 genes in monocytes and/or T cells.
quotes: we found the expected significant enrichment (permutation P < 1 × 10−4) for cis-eQTLs among autoimmune disease–associated variants: Of the 425 GWAS SNPs associated with one or more autoimmune disease, 143 have cis-regulatory effects on 164 genes in monocytes and/or T cells

notes.statement: Okada et al. (2014) performed a trans-ethnic GWAS meta-analysis of 29,880 RA cases and 73,758 controls of European and Asian ancestry, testing about 10 million SNPs. They identified 42 novel RA risk loci at genome-wide significance, which brought the total number of RA risk loci to 101.
quotes: Here we performed a genome-wide association study meta-analysis in a total of >100,000 subjects of European and Asian ancestries (29,880 RA cases and 73,758 controls), by evaluating ∼10 million single-nucleotide polymorphisms. We discovered 42 novel RA risk loci at a genome-wide level of significance, bringing the total to 101 (refs 2 - 4).

notes.statement: Okada et al. (2014) found significant correlations of risk allele frequencies and odds ratios at the 101 RA loci between Europeans and Asians, although 5 loci showed population-specific associations. The 100 non-MHC loci explained 5.5% of heritability in Europeans and 4.7% in Asians. The authors concluded that the genetic risk of RA is generally shared between the 2 populations.
quotes: Comparison of 101 RA risk loci revealed significant correlations of risk allele frequencies (RAF) and odds ratios (OR) between Europeans and Asians (Extended Data Fig. 3a–c; Spearman’s ρ = 0.67 for RAF and 0.76 for OR; P < 1.0×10−13), although 5 loci demonstrated population-specific associations

the 100 RA risk loci outside of the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) region explained 5.5% and 4.7% of heritability in Europeans and Asians, respectively, with 1.6% of the heritability by the novel loci.

notes.statement: Okada et al. (2014) found that RA risk alleles were significantly enriched in H3K4me3 peaks in primary CD4+ regulatory T cells, out of 34 cell types tested. Pathway analysis showed enrichment for T-cell pathways and for B-cell and cytokine signaling pathways (IL10, interferon, GM-CSF).
quotes: Of 34 cell types investigated, we observed significant enrichment of RA risk alleles with trimethylation of histone H3 at lysine 4 (H3K4me3) peaks in primary CD4+ regulatory T cells (Treg cells; P < 1.0×10−5).

We observed enrichment (FDR-q < 0.05) for T cell related pathways, consistent with cell-specific epigenetic marks, as well as enrichment for B cell and cytokine signaling pathways (e.g., IL-10, interferon, GM-CSF).

notes.statement: Okada et al. (2014) found that genes at RA risk loci overlapped significantly with primary immunodeficiency genes (14 of 194), with the highest overlap in the 'immune dysregulation' category. They also overlapped significantly with genes carrying hematologic cancer somatic mutations (17 of 251), but not with genes mutated in nonhematologic cancers.
quotes: Second, we evaluated whether genes from RA risk loci overlapped with PID genes, and observed significant overlap (14/194 = 7.2%, P = 1.2×10−4; Fig. 1a and Extended Data Fig. 5c).
we observed significant overlap with hematological cancers (17/251 = 6.8%, P = 1.2×10−4; Fig. 1b and Extended Data Fig. 5d), but not from non-hematological cancers (6/221 = 2.7%, P = 0.56).

notes.statement: Okada et al. (2014) used an in silico pipeline with 8 criteria to prioritize 98 biological candidate genes among the 377 genes at the 100 non-MHC RA risk loci. These criteria included missense variants, cis-eQTLs, primary immunodeficiency genes, cancer somatic mutation genes, knockout mouse phenotypes and pathway analysis. Sixteen percent of RA risk SNPs were in linkage disequilibrium with missense SNPs, and risk SNPs at 44 loci showed cis-eQTL effects.
quotes: Ninety-eight genes (26.0%) had a score ≥2, which we defined as “candidate biological RA risk genes”.
Sixteen percent of SNPs were in LD with missense SNPs (r2 > 0.80; Extended Data Fig. 5a–b).
we found that RA risk SNPs in 44 loci showed cis-eQTL effects (FDR-q or permutation P < 0.05; Extended Data Table 2).

notes.statement: Okada et al. (2014) found that the targets of approved RA drugs were significantly enriched (3.7-fold) among the biological RA risk genes and their direct protein-protein interaction partners. Examples included tocilizumab, tofacitinib, and abatacept. They proposed that CDK6/CDK4 inhibitors approved for cancer could be repurposed for RA.
quotes: Twenty-seven drug target genes of approved RA drugs demonstrated significant overlap with 98 biological RA risk genes and 2,332 genes from the expanded PPI network (18 genes overlapped; 3.7-fold enrichment by permutation analysis, P < 1.0×10−5; Fig. 3b).
Examples of approved RA therapies identified by this analysis include tocilizumab, (anti-IL6R), tofacitinib (JAK3 inhibitor), and abatacept (CTLA4-Ig; Fig. 3c and Extended Data Fig. 8).
We highlight CDK6 and CDK4, targets of three approved drugs for different types of cancer (Fig. 3d).

notes.statement: Okada et al. (2014) found that about two-thirds of RA risk loci were also associated with other human phenotypes. These included immune-related diseases, inflammatory or hematologic biomarkers, and cardiovascular diseases.
quotes: We found that approximately two-thirds of RA risk loci demonstrated pleiotropy with other human phenotypes (Extended Data Fig. 4), including immune-related diseases (e.g., vitiligo, primary biliary cirrhosis), inflammation-related or hematological biomarkers (e.g., fibrinogen, neutrophil counts) and other complex traits (e.g., cardiovascular diseases).

notes.statement: In a study of 1,115 RA patients and 654 healthy controls, Robinson et al. (2012) used a quantitative sequence variant assay with an adapted paralogue ratio test and found no association of FCGR3A duplications or deletions with RA. They did find overrepresentation of FCGR3B deletions in RA (OR 1.50, P = 0.028), more apparent in rheumatoid factor-positive disease (OR 1.61, P = 0.011).
quotes: to examine independent CNVs carrying FCGR3A and FCGR3B in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) compared with healthy volunteers (n = 1,115 and 654, respectively)

Evidence for association with neither duplications nor deletions of FCGR3A was found; however, in line with previous studies, there was evidence of overrepresentation of FCGR3B deletions in RA (odds ratio [OR] 1.50, P = 0.028), which was more apparent in rheumatoid factor positive disease (OR 1.61, P = 0.011).

notes.statement: Robinson et al. (2012) showed that neutrophil expression of FcgammaRIIIb correlated with FCGR3B gene copy number. They suggested that neutrophils may play an important role in RA pathogenesis, possibly through reduced FcgammaRIIIb-mediated clearance of immune complexes.
quotes: The level of FcγRIIIb, encoded by FCGR3B, expression on neutrophils was shown to correlate with gene copy number.
Thus, our results may highlight an important role for neutrophils in the pathogenesis of RA, potentially through reduced FcγRIIIb-mediated immune complex clearance.

notes.statement: Kurreeman et al. (2011) studied 1,515 RA cases and 1,480 controls drawn from electronic health records and matched for genetic ancestry and anti-citrullinated protein antibody (ACPA) status. In individuals of European ancestry, the odds ratios and the aggregate genetic risk score (GRS) of known RA risk alleles were nearly identical to those from a GWAS of 5,539 autoantibody-positive RA cases and 20,169 controls.
quotes: In 1,515 EHR-derived RA cases and 1,480 controls matched for both genetic ancestry and disease-specific autoantibodies (anti-citrullinated protein antibodies [ACPA]), we demonstrate that the odds ratios and aggregate genetic risk score (GRS) of known RA risk alleles measured in individuals of European ancestry within our EHR cohort are nearly identical to those derived from a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of 5,539 autoantibody-positive RA cases and 20,169 controls.

notes.statement: Kurreeman et al. (2011) found a large overlap in the RA genetic risk score among individuals of European, African, East Asian, and Hispanic ancestry. They concluded that the genetic basis of RA risk is similar across cases of diverse ancestry.
quotes: We extend this approach to other ethnic groups and identify a large overlap in the GRS among individuals of European, African, East Asian, and Hispanic ancestry.
Our study demonstrates that the genetic basis of rheumatoid arthritis risk is similar among cases of diverse ancestry divided into subsets based on ACPA status

notes.statement: Kurreeman et al. (2011) found that the distribution of a genetic risk score based on 28 non-HLA risk alleles in ACPA-positive RA cases partially overlapped with that of the ACPA-negative subgroup of RA cases.
quotes: We also demonstrate that the distribution of a GRS based on 28 non-HLA risk alleles in ACPA+ cases partially overlaps with ACPA- subgroup of RA cases.

notes.statement: Stahl et al. (2010) performed a GWAS meta-analysis of 5,539 autoantibody-positive RA cases and 20,169 controls of European descent. They replicated the findings in 6,768 cases and 8,806 controls and identified 7 new RA risk loci at genome-wide significance (P < 5 x 10(-8)) in the combined analysis of 41,282 samples.
quotes: we conducted a genome-wide association study meta-analysis of 5,539 autoantibody-positive individuals with rheumatoid arthritis (cases) and 20,169 controls of European descent, followed by replication in an independent set of 6,768 rheumatoid arthritis cases and 8,806 controls
Of 34 SNPs selected for replication, 7 new rheumatoid arthritis risk alleles were identified at genome-wide significance (P < 5 x 10(-8)) in an analysis of all 41,282 samples.

notes.statement: Stahl et al. (2010) found 3 RA risk loci that had not been implicated in any earlier genetic study of RA or other autoimmune disease. These were on chromosome 2p14 (rs934734, in intron 1 of SPRED2; P = 5.3 x 10(-10)), 5q11 (rs6859219, in ANKRD55 near IL6ST; P = 9.6 x 10(-12)), and 5q21 (rs26232, in C5orf30; P = 4.1 x 10(-8)).
quotes: The SNPs are located at chromosome 2p14 (rs934734, Poverall=5.3×10−10), 5q11 (rs6859219, Poverall=9.6×10−12) and 5q21 (rs26232, Poverall=4.1×10−8).
At 2p14, the most significant SNP (rs934734) is located within intron 1 of the sprouty-related, EVH1 domain containing 2 (SPRED2) gene
At 5q11, the most significant SNP (rs6859219) is located in ANKRD55, an ankyrin repeat domain-containing gene of unknown function (Figure 1B).

notes.statement: Stahl et al. (2010) found that loci already implicated in other autoimmune diseases were also associated with RA. These were 3p14 near PXK (rs13315591; P = 4.6 x 10(-8)), 4p15 near RBPJ (rs874040; P = 1.0 x 10(-16)), and 6q27 in CCR6 (rs3093023; P = 1.5 x 10(-11)). The IRF5 SNP rs10488631, chosen for its association with SLE, was also associated with RA (P = 4.2 x 10(-11)).
quotes: These 3 SNPs are located at chromosome 3p14 (rs13315591, near PXK, Poverall=4.6×10−8), 4p15 (rs874040, near RBPJ, Poverall=1.0×10−16) and 6q27 (rs3093023, in CCR6, Poverall=1.5×10−11).

The IRF5 SNP rs10488631 (PGWAS =2.8×10−6), chosen because of its association in SLE, was convincingly associated with autoantibody positive RA in our study (Preplication=1.2×10−6, Poverall=4.2×10−11).

notes.statement: Stahl et al. (2010) found new RA-associated alleles at 2 known RA risk loci, with effects at least partly independent of the previously implicated SNPs: CCL21 (rs951005; P = 3.9 x 10(-10)) and IL2RA (rs706778; P = 3.3 x 10(-11)). At IL2RA, RA risk was better explained by the rs2104286(T)-rs11594656(T) haplotype, which confers type 1 diabetes risk, than by rs706778. They also gave definitive evidence for association at AFF3 (rs11676922; P = 1.0 x 10(-14); OR = 1.14).
quotes: Our GWAS meta-analysis identified new alleles exhibiting independent effects from previously implicated RA risk alleles at two other loci, CCL21 (rs951005, Poverall=3.9×10−10) and IL2RA (rs706778, Poverall=3.3×10−11).
conditional and haplotype analyses demonstrated that risk of RA is better explained by this haplotype [rs2104286(T)-rs11594656(T)] than by rs706778
Our study provides definitive evidence that this locus is associated with risk of autoantibody positive RA (rs11676922, Poverall=1.0×10−14, OR=1.14).

notes.statement: At IRF5, Stahl et al. (2010) found that RA was associated with group 1 SNP rs10488631 and with group 3 SNP rs4728142, and that these 2 effects were independent. They found no association with group 2 SNP rs729302. Group 3 SNP rs3807306 was associated with autoantibody-positive RA (P = 4.5 x 10(-6)).
quotes: we found evidence for association with group 3 SNP rs4728142 (PGWAS=7.2×10−6), which is in LD with a variant that alters IRF5 polyadenylation and expression. However, we found no evidence for association for group 2 (rs729302, PGWAS=0.15).
Conditional analyses indicated that the group 1 and group 3 effects are independent

notes.statement: Stahl et al. (2010) estimated that the more than 30 validated non-MHC RA risk alleles explained 3.9% of total disease variance, with 0.67% due to the newly reported alleles. Including an estimated 12% for the MHC, genetic discoveries explained only 16% of disease variance, whereas more than half the risk of autoantibody-positive RA is thought to be genetic.
quotes: We estimate that the now >30 validated non-MHC RA risk alleles explain 3.9% of the total disease variance, with 0.67% due to the new RA risk alleles reported here.
genetic discoveries explain only 16% of disease variance (including an estimated 12% for the MHC), whereas more than half the risk of autoantibody positive RA is thought to be genetic

notes.statement: Stahl et al. (2010) found 11 further SNPs that replicated at P < 0.05 but did not reach genome-wide significance. These included SNPs near IL6R, CD247, IL2/IL21, ZEB1, SH2B3, BATF, CD19/NFATC2IP, IKZF3, UBASH3A, and UBE2L3, and the authors suggested that most were likely genuine RA risk alleles.
quotes: An additional 11 SNPs replicated at P < 0.05, many of which are validated autoimmune risk alleles, suggesting that most represent genuine rheumatoid arthritis risk alleles.

notes.statement: In a genome-wide association study of rheumatoid arthritis in Japanese individuals, Kochi et al. (2010) identified association with a CCR6 polymorphism, rs3093024, at 6q27. They validated the association in two independent Japanese replication cohorts (a total of 7,069 cases and 20,727 controls; overall odds ratio 1.19, P = 7.7 x 10(-19)).
quotes: we identified a polymorphism in CCR6, the gene encoding chemokine (C-C motif) receptor 6 (a surface marker for Th17 cells) at 6q27, that was associated with rheumatoid arthritis susceptibility
rs3093024, a total of 7,069 individuals with rheumatoid arthritis (cases) and 20,727 controls, overall odds ratio = 1.19, P = 7.7 x 10(-19)

notes.statement: Kochi et al. (2010) identified a triallelic dinucleotide polymorphism in CCR6 (CCR6DNP) that was in strong linkage disequilibrium with rs3093024 and affected gene transcription. The CCR6DNP genotype correlated with CCR6 expression level and was associated with the presence of IL-17 in the sera of patients with rheumatoid arthritis. The authors suggested that CCR6 is critically involved in IL-17-driven autoimmunity.
quotes: We identified a triallelic dinucleotide polymorphism of CCR6 (CCR6DNP) in strong linkage disequilibrium with rs3093024 that showed effects on gene transcription.
The CCR6DNP genotype was correlated with the expression level of CCR6 and was associated with the presence of interleukin-17 (IL-17) in the sera of subjects with rheumatoid arthritis.
These results suggest that CCR6 is critically involved in IL-17-driven autoimmunity in human diseases.

notes.statement: Kochi et al. (2010) found that CCR6DNP was also associated with susceptibility to Graves disease and Crohn disease.
quotes: Moreover, CCR6DNP was associated with susceptibility to Graves' and Crohn's diseases.

notes.statement: In a genome-wide association study of common CNVs in about 2,000 cases of each of 8 common diseases, including rheumatoid arthritis, and 3,000 shared controls, Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium et al. (2010) found CNVs in the HLA region associated with rheumatoid arthritis (CNVR2845.14, p = 1.4 x 10(-39), odds ratio 1.77). They had no evidence that these HLA CNVs were signals independent of the known associated HLA haplotypes.
quotes: We observed CNVs in the HLA region associated variously with Crohn's disease (CNVR2841.20, p= 1.2 × 10−5, OR = 0.80), rheumatoid arthritis (CNVR2845.14, p= 1.4 × 10−39, OR = 1.77), and type 1 diabetes (CNVR2845.46, p= 8 × 10−153, OR = 0.2).
we have no evidence that suggests that the HLA CNVs associated with autoimmune diseases in this study represent signals independent of the known associated haplotypes.

notes.statement: Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium et al. (2010) found that CNVR1065.1 is annotated as mapping to chromosome 2 but is actually a dispersed duplication with its polymorphism located in the HLA region. It showed a strong signal in rheumatoid arthritis and type 1 diabetes and was well tagged by HLA SNPs known to be associated with both diseases.
quotes: We found one similar example, of a CNV (CNVR1065.1, featuring in Table 2 as a replicated association) annotated as mapping uniquely to chromosome 2 which shows a strong signal in type 1 diabetes and rheumatoid arthritis.
Careful examination shows it to be another dispersed duplication where the polymorphism is located in the HLA, and is well tagged by HLA SNPs known to be associated with both diseases.

notes.statement: Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium et al. (2010) found no significant association of the multiallelic CNVs at CCL3L1, beta-defensin, or FCGR3A/B with rheumatoid arthritis after correction for multiple testing. In particular, they did not formally replicate the reported association between CCL3L1 and rheumatoid arthritis (nominal p = 0.058).
quotes: None of the CNVs shows significant association with the three autoimmune diseases in our study after allowance for multiple testing. In particular, we do not see formally significant evidence to replicate the reported association for CCL3L1 and rheumatoid arthritis (nominal p = 0.058).

notes.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2009) used GRAIL, a text-mining method, to score 179 loci with P < 0.001 in a published RA GWAS meta-analysis (3,393 cases and 12,462 controls) for functional relationships to genes in 16 known RA loci. They genotyped the 22 loci that scored significantly in 7,957 autoantibody-positive cases and 11,958 matched controls of European ancestry.
quotes: We used Gene Relationships Across Implicated Loci (GRAIL), a computational method that applies statistical text mining to PubMed abstracts, to score these 179 loci for functional relationships to genes in 16 established RA disease loci.
We identified 22 loci with a significant degree of functional connectivity. We genotyped 22 representative SNPs in an independent set of 7,957 cases and 11,958 matched controls.

notes.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2009) confirmed 3 new RA risk loci at genomewide significance: rs11586238 on 1p13.1 near CD2 and CD58 (overall P = 1.0 x 10(-9)), rs1980422 on 2q33.2 near CD28 (overall P = 1.3 x 10(-9)), and rs548234 on 6q21 near PRDM1 (overall P = 2.1 x 10(-8)).
quotes: we observed the strongest associations at rs11586238 on 1p13.1 near the CD2 and CD58 genes (1.4×10−6 replication, 1.0×10−9 overall), at rs1980422 on 2q33.2 near CD28 (4.7×10−6 replication, 1.3×10−9 overall), and at rs548234 on 6q21 near PRDM1 (1.2×10−5 replication, 2.1×10−8 overall).

notes.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2009) found 4 more loci that replicated but did not reach a conservative genomewide threshold in the combined analysis: rs394581 near TAGAP on 6q25.3 (overall P = 3.8 x 10(-7)), rs10919563 in a PTPRC intron on 1q31.3 (overall P = 6.7 x 10(-7)), rs540386 in a TRAF6 intron on 11p12 (overall P = 3.9 x 10(-6)), and rs12746613 near FCGR2A on 1q23.3 (overall P = 1.5 x 10(-5)). They concluded these likely represent true RA loci.
quotes: We observed evidence of association at rs394581 on 6q25.3 near TAGAP (1.5×10−4 replication, 3.8×10−7 overall), rs10919563 on 1q31.3 within a PTPRC intron (2.6×10−4 replication, 6.7×10−7 overall), rs540386 on 11p12 within a TRAF6 intron (8.3×10−4 replication, 3.9×10−6 overall), and rs12746613 on 1q23.3 near FCGR2A (2.2×10−3 replication, 1.5×10−5 overall).
These SNP associations likely represent true RA loci, but additional genotyping will be necessary for definitive confirmation.

notes.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2009) found that the CD28 SNP rs1980422 lies 129 kb from the known RA risk allele rs3087243 in the CTLA4 region and is in minimal linkage disequilibrium with it. Conditional analysis confirmed that the two SNPs confer RA risk independently.
quotes: The rs1980422 SNP is located about 10 kb away from the 3′ UTR of CD28 and is 129 kb away from a known RA and type I diabetes risk allele in the CTLA4 region (rs3087243).
There is minimal LD between these two SNPs (r2=0.04, D’=0.40); conditional analysis confirmed that the two SNPs independently confer RA risk

notes.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2009) found no significant epistatic interactions among the 7 replicated SNPs and the known RA risk alleles. The 7 associations had consistent effects across all 14 collections, with no evidence of heterogeneity.
quotes: We examined all 7 replicated RA SNPs along with known RA risk alleles for epistatic interactions (see Supplementary Note online). Despite the functional relationships between these genes, we found no evidence of significant interactions.
our seven replicated SNP associations demonstrate consistent effects across all 14 collections without evidence of heterogeneity

notes.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2009) concluded that the new loci further implicate T-cell activation, NF-kappa-B signaling, and B-cell activation and differentiation in RA. The PRDM1 (BLIMP1) locus pointed to a new process: terminal differentiation of B cells into plasma cells. They noted that functional studies would be needed to confirm the causal genes.
quotes: These SNP associations continue to clarify critical biological processes involved in RA pathogenesis, including T-cell activation, NF-κB signaling, and B-cell activation and differentiation.
Our study has also implicated novel processes represented by PRDM1 (BLIMP-1), a transcription factor that regulates terminal differentiation of B-cells into immunoglobulin secreting plasma cells.

notes.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2009) noted that several of the new RA loci lie near alleles associated with other autoimmune diseases. These include FCGR2A (systemic lupus erythematosus), TAGAP (celiac disease and type 1 diabetes), PTPRC and CD58 (multiple sclerosis), and PRDM1 (Crohn disease). However, none of the RA risk alleles corresponded perfectly to a previously established autoimmune allele.
quotes: Many of these seven alleles further implicate genomic regions already associated with autoimmune diseases (see Table 3). At this point none of these RA risk alleles correspond perfectly to any previously established autoimmune allele

notes.statement: In 1,497 individuals from 3 RA cohorts, Mahdi et al. (2009) detected antibodies to the immunodominant citrullinated alpha-enolase CEP-1 epitope in 43 to 63% of anti-CCP-positive individuals. This subset was preferentially linked to HLA-DRB1*04.
quotes: In 1,497 individuals from three RA cohorts, antibodies to the immunodominant citrullinated alpha-enolase CEP-1 epitope were detected in 43-63% of the anti-CCP-positive individuals, and this subset was preferentially linked to HLA-DRB1*04.

notes.statement: In a case-control analysis of 1,000 RA patients and 872 controls, Mahdi et al. (2009) found that the combined effect of the HLA-DRB1 shared epitope, PTPN22 and smoking was most strongly associated with the anti-CEP-1-positive subset (OR, 37). The OR was only 2 for the corresponding anti-CEP-1-negative, anti-CCP-positive subset. They concluded that citrullinated alpha-enolase is a specific citrullinated autoantigen that links smoking to genetic risk factors in the development of RA.
quotes: In a case-control analysis of 1,000 affected individuals and 872 controls, the combined effect of shared epitope, PTPN22 and smoking showed the strongest association with the anti-CEP-1-positive subset (odds ratio (OR) of 37, compared to an OR of 2 for the corresponding anti-CEP-1-negative, anti-CCP-positive subset).
We conclude that citrullinated alpha-enolase is a specific citrullinated autoantigen that links smoking to genetic risk factors in the development of RA.

notes.statement: In a genome-wide association study of 2,418 rheumatoid arthritis cases and 4,504 controls from North America, Gregersen et al. (2009) identified an association at the REL locus on chromosome 2p13 (rs13031237, P = 6.01 x 10(-10)). After PTPN22, this was the second most significant non-MHC association.
quotes: We conducted a genome-wide association study of rheumatoid arthritis in 2,418 cases and 4,504 controls from North America and identified an association at the REL locus, encoding c-Rel, on chromosome 2p13 (rs13031237, P = 6.01 x 10(-10)).
However, after PTPN22 the second most significant association is observed on chromosome 2 in the region of REL

notes.statement: Gregersen et al. (2009) replicated the REL association in 2,604 cases and 2,882 controls. In the combined dataset, the allelic OR was 1.25 (P = 3.08 x 10(-14)) for rs13031237 and 1.21 (P = 2.60 x 10(-11)) for rs13017599.
quotes: Replication in independent case-control datasets comprising 2,604 cases and 2,882 controls confirmed this association, yielding an allelic OR = 1.25 (P = 3.08 x 10(-14)) for marker rs13031237 and an allelic OR = 1.21 (P = 2.60 x 10(-11)) for marker rs13017599 in the combined dataset.

notes.statement: In the combined dataset, Gregersen et al. (2009) found definitive support for associations of rheumatoid arthritis with CTLA4 (rs231735; OR = 0.85; P = 6.25 x 10(-9)) and BLK (rs2736340; OR = 1.19; P = 5.69 x 10(-9)). Genotype-specific results showed codominance at all loci except CTLA4, which was nearly dominant. No significant gene-gene interactions were found after correction for multiple testing.
quotes: The combined dataset also provides definitive support for associations at both CTLA4 (rs231735; OR = 0.85; P = 6.25 x 10(-9)) and BLK (rs2736340; OR = 1.19; P = 5.69 x 10(-9)).
Supplementary table 4 presents genotype-specific results, which show codominance for all the loci except CTLA4, which is nearly dominant.
Given that 471 tests were performed, no significant interaction effects were identified, after correcting for multiple testing.

notes.statement: In their genome-wide scan, Gregersen et al. (2009) confirmed the strongest association in the MHC region (P = 9.50 x 10(-104)). They also confirmed previously reported associations at PTPN22 (rs2476601, P = 1.62 x 10(-21)) and the TRAF1/C5 region (rs881375, P = 4.09 x 10(-8)).
quotes: the largest association signal is in an extended region within the MHC achieving a maximal level significance of p=9.50 × 10-104 in this study.
the previously reported associations are confirmed at PTPN22 (rs2476601, p= 1.62 × 10-21) and the TRAF1/C5 regions (maximal association at rs881375, p= 4.09×10-8).

notes.statement: Gregersen et al. (2009) suggested that the association of REL with rheumatoid arthritis points to disease pathways involving other RA susceptibility genes, including CD40, TRAF1, TNFAIP3, and PRKCQ. They proposed that CD40 signaling pathways have an important role in RA pathogenesis.
quotes: c-Rel is an NF-kappaB family member with distinct functional properties in hematopoietic cells, and its association with rheumatoid arthritis suggests disease pathways that involve other recently identified rheumatoid arthritis susceptibility genes including CD40, TRAF1, TNFAIP3 and PRKCQ.
The associations of CD40, REL, TRAF1 and TNFAIP3 are consistent with an important role for CD40 signaling pathways in RA pathogenesis.

notes.statement: Gregersen et al. (2009) noted that antibodies to cyclic citrullinated peptides (CCP) are a highly sensitive and specific diagnostic marker for RA, present in 50 to 80% of patients who meet standard criteria. The classic HLA-DRB1 associations are restricted to this subgroup.
quotes: the presence of which is a highly sensitive and specific marker for the diagnosis of RA; between 50 and 80% of patients meeting standard criteria for RA exhibit anti-CCP antibodies.
Remarkably, the classical HLA-DRB1 associations with RA are entirely restricted to this phenotypic subgroup

notes.statement: Orozco et al. (2009) fine-mapped 70 SNPs at 6q23 in 3,962 UK RA patients and 3,531 controls and found 18 SNPs associated with RA. The strongest association was with rs6920220 (P = 2.6 x 10(-6), OR 1.22). The next strongest was rs13207033 (P = 0.0001, OR 0.86), which was perfectly correlated with rs10499194; the authors described this as the first independent replication of that SNP.
quotes: 3962 RA patients and 3531 healthy controls were included in the study. We found 18 SNPs associated with RA. The SNP showing the strongest association was rs6920220 [P = 2.6 x 10(-6), OR (95% CI) 1.22 (1.13-1.33)].
This represents the first independent replication of the association of the rs10499194 polymorphism with RA susceptibility.

notes.statement: In conditional logistic regression, Orozco et al. (2009) found that three SNPs stayed significant: rs6920220, rs13207033 (protective) and rs5029937 in intron 2 of TNFAIP3. Carrying the risk alleles of both rs6920220 and rs5029937 without the protective allele of rs13207033 gave an OR of 1.86 compared with carrying none. This equated to an effect size of 1.50 compared with controls. The authors noted that replication of the rs5029937 effect in an independent cohort was required.
quotes: Of the 18 associated SNPs, three polymorphisms, rs6920220, rs13207033 and rs5029937, remained significant after conditional logistic regression analysis.

The combination of the carriage of both risk alleles of rs6920220 and rs5029937 together with the absence of the protective allele of rs13207033 was strongly associated with RA when compared with carriage of none [OR of 1.86 (95% CI) (1.51-2.29)].
The results provide convincing evidence to support a third allele in the 6q23 region but replication in an independent cohort is required to confirm this unequivocally.

notes.statement: Orozco et al. (2009) found that rs6920220 and rs5029937 were associated with autoantibody-positive RA, both RF-positive and anti-CCP-positive. In contrast, rs13207033 was associated with both RF-positive and RF-negative RA, but only with anti-CCP-negative RA.
quotes: rs6920220 and the intron 2 SNP, rs5029937, appeared to be associated with auto-antibody positive cases, with strong association in both RF positive and anti-CCP positive cases. In contrast, rs13207033 was associated with both RF positive and negative RA cases, but only anti-CCP negative cases.

notes.statement: Barton et al. (2009) genotyped 18 SNPs from 14 putative type 1 diabetes susceptibility loci in 3,962 UK RA cases and 3,531 controls. They found a new RA susceptibility locus at AFF3. In a combined analysis of 6,819 RA cases and 12,650 controls, rs10865035 was associated with RA (OR 1.12, 95% CI 1.07-1.17, P = 2.8 x 10(-7)).
quotes: A novel RA susceptibility locus at AFF3 was identified with convincing evidence for association in a combined sample cohort of 6819 RA cases and 12 650 controls [OR 1.12 95% confidence intervals (CI) 1.07-1.17, P = 2.8 x 10(-7)].
Eighteen single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) mapping to 14 distinct loci were genotyped in 3962 UK RA cases and 3531 unrelated UK controls.

notes.statement: Barton et al. (2009) found that the associated AFF3 variants mapped to the 5-prime and promoter region of the AFF3 gene. AFF3 is preferentially expressed in lymphoid cells and encodes a nuclear factor with transcriptional activation domains, which the authors considered made it a strong candidate autoimmunity gene.
quotes: The associated variants map to the 5′ and promoter region of the AFF3 gene, which is strongly conserved in evolution and is preferentially expressed in lymphoid cells. It encodes a nuclear factor that can interact with DNA and contains transcriptional activation domains, making it a strong candidate autoimmunity gene.

notes.statement: Barton et al. (2009) replicated the association of RA with the CTLA4 SNP rs3087243 (OR 0.87, P = 1.1 x 10(-4)). In a meta-analysis that combined their data with 2 earlier well-powered studies, the association was confirmed (OR 0.88, P = 2.6 x 10(-6)).
quotes: A variant mapping to the CTLA-4 gene showed the strongest evidence for association with RA in the current cohort (rs3087243 OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.82–0.94, P = 1.1 × 10−4).
Combining the results from two previous well-powered studies with the current data, the SNP is confirmed as being associated with RA susceptibility [OR 0.88 (0.83–0.93), P = 2.6 × 10−6] (Fig. 1).

notes.statement: Barton et al. (2009) replicated the association of RA with rs6822844 in the IL2-IL21 region on chromosome 4q27. The common allele predisposed to disease (OR 0.86, P = 5.4 x 10(-4)).
quotes: As reported previously, it was the common allele that predisposed to disease [rs6822844 OR 0.86, (0.79–0.94), P = 5.4 × 10−4].

notes.statement: Barton et al. (2009) stratified RA patients by rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibody status. The strength of association at the AFF3, CTLA4, and 4q27 SNPs was similar in autoantibody-positive and autoantibody-negative patients.
quotes: However, following stratification by presence of auto-antibodies, the strength of associations was similar between auto-antibody positive and negative individuals at all three SNPs indicated by the overlapping confidence intervals (Table 2).

notes.statement: Barton et al. (2009) found that the common allele of the IL7R SNP rs6897932 showed a trend toward association with RA (OR 0.90, P = 0.007). This did not reach their corrected significance threshold.
quotes: Finally, although the common allele of a non-synonymous SNP (rs6897932) mapping to the IL7R gene previously associated with both T1D and multiple sclerosis was somewhat over-represented in RA cases (OR 0.90, 95% CI 0.84–0.97; trend P = 0.007), this did not achieve statistical significance at the corrected P-value threshold.

notes.statement: Barton et al. (2009) stated that 13 loci had been confirmed as associated with RA susceptibility: HLA-DRB1, PTPN22, STAT4, TRAF1/C5, 6q23, IL2RB, 12q13, 10p15, CD40, MMEL1, AFF3, 4q27, and CTLA4. All but TRAF1/C5 had also been associated with other autoimmune diseases.
quotes: so that a total of 13 loci have now been confirmed as associated with RA susceptibility (HLA DRB1, PTPN22, STAT4, TRAF1/C5, 6q23, IL2RB, 12q13, 10p15, CD40, MMEL1, AFF3, 4q27 and CTLA-4).
Interestingly, for all but one of these loci (TRAF1/C5), association with other autoimmune diseases, including systemic lupus erythematosus, Graves disease and coeliac disease, has been described

notes.statement: Suzuki et al. (2008) identified a linkage disequilibrium block on chromosome 1q containing multiple SLAM family genes that was associated with rheumatoid arthritis. The association peaked at 2 functional SNPs in CD244, rs3766379 and rs6682654, in 2 independent Japanese RA cohorts (P = 3.23 x 10(-8) and P = 7.45 x 10(-8)).
quotes: We identified a linkage disequilibrium block associated with rheumatoid arthritis in the chromosome 1q region containing multiple SLAM family genes.
In this block, the association peaked at two functional SNPs (rs3766379 and rs6682654) in CD244 in two independent rheumatoid arthritis cohorts from Japan (P = 3.23 x 10(-8) and P = 7.45 x 10(-8)).

notes.statement: Suzuki et al. (2008) found that a Japanese cohort with systemic lupus erythematosus had a genotype distribution at CD244 similar to that of the RA cohorts, suggesting that CD244 may have a role in an autoimmune process shared by RA and SLE.
quotes: We also identified a Japanese cohort with systemic lupus erythematosus that had a similar genotype distribution as the rheumatoid arthritis cohorts.
CD244 is a genetic risk factor for rheumatoid arthritis and may have a role in the autoimmune process shared by rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus.

notes.statement: Suzuki et al. (2008) showed in luciferase and allele-specific transcript quantification assays that the RA-susceptible alleles of rs3766379 and rs6682654 in CD244, and their haplotype, increased expression.
quotes: We demonstrated that the rheumatoid arthritis-susceptible alleles of rs3766379 and rs6682654 and their haplotype increased their expression in luciferase and allele-specific transcript quantification assays.

notes.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2008) combined 2 published GWA studies of European rheumatoid arthritis in a meta-analysis (3,393 cases, 12,462 controls). They then tested 31 top-ranked SNPs in a replication set of 3,929 autoantibody-positive cases and 5,807 matched controls drawn from 8 collections. They found a common variant at the CD40 locus on chromosome 20q13 (rs4810485) that reached P = 8.2 x 10(-9) overall, with an odds ratio of 0.87.
quotes: we conducted a meta-analysis of two published genome-wide association (GWA) studies totaling 3,393 cases and 12,462 controls
We identified a common variant at the CD40 gene locus (rs4810485, P = 0.0032 replication, P = 8.2 x 10(-9) overall, OR = 0.87).

notes.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2008) reported that rs4810485 lies in the second intron of CD40. It is in near-perfect linkage disequilibrium (r2 = 0.95) with rs1883832, a variant that disrupts a Kozak sequence and has been shown to affect how efficiently CD40 protein is translated. The authors concluded that this points to a putative functional variant and supports a central role for the CD40 signaling pathway in autoantibody-positive rheumatoid arthritis.
quotes: This SNP is located in the second intron of CD40 and is within an LD block that contains a large portion of the CD40 gene and its 5′ intergenic region.
The rs1883832 variant has been shown to influence the efficiency of CD40 protein translation by disrupting a Kozak sequence.
These associations provide strong evidence for the importance of the CD40 signaling pathway in autoantibody-positive rheumatoid arthritis.

notes.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2008) also found an association at the CCL21 locus on 9p13 (rs2812378; replication P = 0.00097, overall P = 2.8 x 10(-7)). The SNP lies about 0.1 kb from the CCL21 5-prime UTR, in an LD block that contains the CCL21 coding sequence.
quotes: We also identified association at the CCL21 gene locus (rs2812378, P = 0.00097 replication, P = 2.8 x 10(-7) overall), a gene involved in lymphocyte trafficking.
The SNP is located ~0.1 kb from the 5′ untranslated region of the CCL21 gene

notes.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2008) found evidence of association at 4 more loci: MMEL1-TNFRSF14 (rs3890745, overall P = 1.1 x 10(-7)), CDK6 (rs42041, P = 4.0 x 10(-6)), PRKCQ (rs4750316, P = 4.4 x 10(-6)) and KIF5A-PIP4K2C (rs1678542, P = 8.8 x 10(-8)). The authors noted that these associations still needed further validation.
quotes: Finally, we identified evidence of association at four additional gene loci: MMEL1-TNFRSF14 (rs3890745, P = 0.0035 replication, P = 1.1 x 10(-7) overall), CDK6 (rs42041, P = 0.010 replication, P = 4.0 x 10(-6) overall), PRKCQ (rs4750316, P = 0.0078 replication, P = 4.4 x 10(-6) overall), and KIF5A-PIP4K2C (rs1678542, P = 0.0026 replication, P = 8.8 x 10(-8) overall).

notes.statement: In their GWA meta-analysis, Raychaudhuri et al. (2008) confirmed associations at PTPN22, 6q23 (TNFAIP3), STAT4 and TRAF1-C5. They also observed association at 4q27 (IL2/IL21) and CTLA4 but not at PADI4.
quotes: Of the confirmed non-MHC risk loci, we observed association at PTPN22, 6q23/(containing TNFAIP3), STAT4 and TRAF1-C5. We also observed evidence of association at 4q27 (containing the IL2 and IL21 genes) and CTLA4, but not PADI4.

notes.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2008) estimated that all known non-MHC common variants together explain only 3.6% of the variance in rheumatoid arthritis risk. Because about 60% of risk is thought to be genetic, they concluded that known risk alleles account for less than half of the genetic variation, and that more common alleles of modest effect probably remain to be found.
quotes: In this study, we estimate that the total percent variance explained for all known non-MHC common genetic variants is just 3.6%.

Considering that ~60% of rheumatoid arthritis risk is thought to be genetic, and one-third of this risk is from the MHC locus, this indicates that less than half of genetic variation can be explained by the known rheumatoid arthritis risk alleles.

notes.statement: Martínez et al. (2008) genotyped the STAT4 tagging SNP rs7574865 in 575 Spanish patients with rheumatoid arthritis and 723 ethnically matched controls and confirmed the association of the T allele with RA (P = 1.2 x 10(-6); OR 1.59, 95% CI 1.31-1.92). The same variant was also associated with inflammatory bowel disease and type 1 diabetes, but not with multiple sclerosis. The authors concluded that STAT4 is emerging as a common risk factor for diverse complex diseases.
quotes: The association of STAT4 polymorphism rs7574865 with RA was validated in patients of Spanish origin (for T versus G, P = 1.2 x 10(-6), odds ratio [OR] 1.59, 95% confidence interval [95% CI] 1.31-1.92)
In contrast, the genotypic distribution of this polymorphism showed no difference between patients with multiple sclerosis and healthy control subjects
The STAT4 gene is emerging as a novel common risk factor for diverse complex diseases.

notes.statement: Plenge et al. (2007) genotyped 397 individuals with rheumatoid arthritis for 116,204 SNPs and compared them with 1,211 related individuals from the Framingham Heart Study. They identified a SNP at 6q23 (rs10499194), about 150 kb from TNFAIP3 and OLIG3, that was associated with rheumatoid arthritis. The association was reproducible in 5,541 additional case-control samples (P = 10(-3) in the GWA scan, P < 10(-6) in replication, and P = 10(-9) combined).
quotes: we genotyped 397 individuals with rheumatoid arthritis for 116,204 SNPs and carried out an association analysis in comparison to publicly available genotype data for 1,211 related individuals from the Framingham Heart Study

we identified a SNP at 6q23 (rs10499194, approximately 150 kb from TNFAIP3 and OLIG3) that was reproducibly associated with rheumatoid arthritis both in the genome-wide association (GWA) scan and in 5,541 additional case-control samples (P = 10(-3), GWA scan; P < 10(-6), replication; P = 10(-9), combined)

notes.statement: Plenge et al. (2007) showed that rs10499194 and rs6920220 are statistically independent. rs6920220 lies 3.8 kb from rs10499194 and had been reported by the Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium (WTCCC). Each association was reproducible when their data were compared with WTCCC data, and together the two SNPs defined risk and protective haplotypes for rheumatoid arthritis at 6q23.
quotes: the Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium (WTCCC) has reported strong association of rheumatoid arthritis susceptibility to a different SNP located 3.8 kb from rs10499194 (rs6920220; P = 5 x 10(-6) in WTCCC)

We show that these two SNP associations are statistically independent, are each reproducible in the comparison of our data and WTCCC data, and define risk and protective haplotypes for rheumatoid arthritis at 6q23.

notes.statement: Thomson et al. (2007) genotyped 10 SNPs, including 9 newly suggested by the WTCCC genome-wide association screen, in an independent UK cohort of 5,063 rheumatoid arthritis cases and 3,849 controls. They replicated the association of rs6920220 (G>A) at 6q23 (minor-allele OR = 1.23, trend P = 1.1 x 10(-8)). In the combined WTCCC and validation data, the OR was 1.22 (trend P = 3.6 x 10(-12)).
quotes: Of the nine newly identified SNPs tested, rs6920220 (G > A) showed association with rheumatoid arthritis in this cohort (OR for minor allele = 1.23, 95% CI = 1.15-1.33, trend P = 1.1 × 10-8) (Table 1).
we obtained strong statistical evidence for association between this SNP and rheumatoid arthritis (OR = 1.22, 95% CI = 1.15-1.29, trend P = 3.6 × 10-12) (Table 1).

notes.statement: Thomson et al. (2007) found that rs6920220 lay in an intergenic linkage-disequilibrium block of about 60 kb at 6q23. The block contained no known genes but included part of a PTPN11 pseudogene and lay between OLIG3 and TNFAIP3. The authors noted that TNFAIP3, a negative regulator of NF-kappa-B, was a plausible candidate, because TNFAIP3-deficient mice develop multiorgan inflammation that includes the joints.
quotes: all five SNPs map to a single linkage-disequilibrium block spanning 60 kb (Supplementary Fig. 1 online). The block contains no known genes or transcripts but does encompass part of the PTPN11 pseudogene.
The block lies between the genes OLIG3 and TNFAIP3 (also known as A20).
Mice deficient for the TNFAIP3 protein developed multiorgan inflammation, including inflammation of joints.

notes.statement: Thomson et al. (2007) found that the rs6920220 association was stronger in anti-CCP-positive and rheumatoid factor-positive patients than in antibody-negative patients. The difference between the anti-CCP-positive and anti-CCP-negative subgroups was significant (trend P = 0.003). The authors said this supported the idea that rheumatoid arthritis comprises at least two genetically distinct subsets.
quotes: Analysis of the WTCCC study indicated a significant association for SNP rs6920220 in anti-CCP-positive (OR = 1.38, 95% CI = 1.22-1.55, trend P = 1.7 × 10-7) but not in anti-CCP-negative individuals (OR = 1.03, 95% CI = 0.82-1.29).
Indeed, the difference between the anti-CCP-positive and negative subgroups was statistically significant (trend P = 0.003).

notes.statement: Thomson et al. (2007) found no evidence of interaction between rs6920220 and the HLA-DRB1 or PTPN22 susceptibility markers. Together, the HLA-DRB1 shared epitope, PTPN22 rs2476601 and rs6920220 accounted for 8.5% of the total variance in rheumatoid arthritis susceptibility. They also confirmed the association with PTPN22 rs2476601 (OR = 1.53, trend P = 2.0 x 10(-18)).
quotes: We did not detect evidence for interaction with HLA-DRB1 or PTPN22 susceptibility markers, suggesting that the rs6920220 variant confers an additional effect independent of the two known susceptibility genes.
Together, HLA-DRB1 (shared epitope), PTPN22 (rs2476601) and rs6920220 account for 8.5% of the total variance in rheumatoid arthritis susceptibility.
We detected strong association with the rheumatoid arthritis-causing SNP in the PTPN22 gene (rs2476601), as expected (odds ratio (OR) = 1.53, 95% CI = 1.39-1.68, trend P = 2.0 × 10-18).

notes.statement: Thomson et al. (2007) found only modest evidence for association of rs743777 in IL2RB (combined trend P = 5.3 x 10(-6)) and borderline evidence for rs11761231 near PODXL (trend P = 0.042). rs2104286 in IL2RA was not associated with rheumatoid arthritis in their dataset.
quotes: In the combined cohort analysis, this SNP showed modest evidence for association (OR = 1.13, 95% CI = 1.07-1.19; trend P = 5.3 × 10-6), suggesting the effect, if any, is weak.

Notably, rs2104286, which maps to IL2RA, a gene already associated with a number of other autoimmune diseases (type 1 diabetes, multiple sclerosis and Graves’ disease) and known to play a role in T cell regulation, was not associated with rheumatoid arthritis in this dataset.

notes.statement: In 1,620 North American patients with established rheumatoid arthritis and 2,635 controls, Remmers et al. (2007) tested SNPs in and around 13 candidate genes in the previously linked chromosome 2q region and fine-mapped the STAT1-STAT4 region. A SNP haplotype in the third intron of STAT4 was associated with susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis.
quotes: We tested single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in and around 13 candidate genes within the previously linked chromosome 2q region for association with rheumatoid arthritis.
A SNP haplotype in the third intron of STAT4 was associated with susceptibility to both rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus.

notes.statement: Remmers et al. (2007) found the minor alleles of the haplotype-defining STAT4 SNPs on 27% of chromosomes from patients with established rheumatoid arthritis, compared with 22% from controls (for rs7574865, P = 2.81 x 10(-7); odds ratio 1.32). The association was replicated in 1,529 Swedish patients with early rheumatoid arthritis and 881 controls (P = 0.02). Homozygosity for the risk allele, compared with absence of the allele, was associated with a 60% increased risk of rheumatoid arthritis.
quotes: The minor alleles of the haplotype-defining SNPs were present in 27% of chromosomes of patients with established rheumatoid arthritis, as compared with 22% of those of controls (for the SNP rs7574865, P=2.81x10(-7); odds ratio for having the risk allele in chromosomes of patients vs. those of controls, 1.32).
The association was replicated in Swedish patients with recent-onset rheumatoid arthritis (P=0.02) and matched controls.
Homozygosity of the risk allele, as compared with absence of the allele, was associated with a more than doubled risk for lupus and a 60% increased risk for rheumatoid arthritis.

notes.statement: Remmers et al. (2007) found that the same STAT4 haplotype was strongly associated with systemic lupus erythematosus (31% vs 22% of chromosomes; P = 1.87 x 10(-9); odds ratio 1.55). They suggested that rheumatoid arthritis and lupus share a pathway.
quotes: The haplotype marked by rs7574865 was strongly associated with lupus, being present on 31% of chromosomes of case patients and 22% of those of controls (P=1.87x10(-9); odds ratio for having the risk allele in chromosomes of patients vs. those of controls, 1.55).
A haplotype of STAT4 is associated with increased risk for both rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus, suggesting a shared pathway for these illnesses.

notes.statement: In a genomewide association study, Plenge et al. (2007) genotyped 317,503 SNPs in 1,522 anti-CCP-positive rheumatoid arthritis cases and 1,850 matched controls from the NARAC and Swedish EIRA cohorts. They found an association with a SNP on chromosome 9, rs3761847, that held in all samples tested, including an independent replication set. The odds ratio was 1.32 (95% CI, 1.23-1.42; P = 4 x 10(-14)).
quotes: We genotyped 317,503 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in a combined case-control study of 1522 case subjects with rheumatoid arthritis and 1850 matched control subjects.
in a SNP (rs3761847) on chromosome 9 for all samples tested, the latter with an odds ratio of 1.32 (95% confidence interval, 1.23 to 1.42; P=4x10(-14))

notes.statement: Plenge et al. (2007) noted that rs3761847 is in linkage disequilibrium with 2 genes relevant to chronic inflammation, TRAF1 and C5. They concluded that a common variant at the TRAF1-C5 locus is associated with an increased risk of anti-CCP-positive rheumatoid arthritis. The same study also confirmed associations with the MHC locus and with PTPN22.
quotes: The SNP is in linkage disequilibrium with two genes relevant to chronic inflammation: TRAF1 (encoding tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factor 1) and C5 (encoding complement component 5).
A common genetic variant at the TRAF1-C5 locus on chromosome 9 is associated with an increased risk of anti-CCP-positive rheumatoid arthritis.
We observed associations between disease and variants in the major-histocompatibility-complex locus, in PTPN22

notes.statement: Sigurdsson et al. (2007) analyzed 5 SNPs in IRF5 and 3 SNPs in TYK2 in a Swedish cohort of 1,530 patients with RA and 881 controls. Four of the 5 SNPs in the 5-prime region of IRF5 were associated with RA. None of the TYK2 SNPs were associated.
quotes: Five single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in IRF5 and 3 SNPs in Tyk2 were analyzed in a Swedish cohort of 1,530 patients with RA and 881 controls.
Four of the 5 SNPs located in the 5' region of IRF5 were associated with RA, while no association was observed with the Tyk2 SNPs.

notes.statement: Sigurdsson et al. (2007) found that the minor alleles of 3 IRF5 SNPs were in linkage disequilibrium. Together they formed a relatively common haplotype (frequency about 0.33) that appeared to protect against RA. The association was seen mainly in anti-CCP-negative patients. A suggestive association with anti-CCP-negative RA was also seen in a Dutch replication cohort of 387 patients and 181 controls.
quotes: The minor alleles of 3 of the IRF5 SNPs, which were in linkage disequilibrium and formed a relatively common haplotype with a frequency of approximately 0.33, appeared to confer protection against RA.

Although these disease associations were seen in the entire patient group, they were mainly found in RA patients who were negative for anti-CCP. A suggestive association of IRF5 SNPs with anti-CCP-negative RA was also observed in the Dutch cohort.

notes.statement: Sigurdsson et al. (2007) concluded that genetic variants of IRF5 contribute to a unique disease etiology and pathogenesis in anti-CCP-negative RA. They noted that this subset differs from anti-CCP-positive RA in its genetic and environmental risk factors.
quotes: Given the fact that anti-CCP-negative RA differs from anti-CCP-positive RA with respect to genetic and environmental risk factor profiles, our results indicate that genetic variants of IRF5 contribute to a unique disease etiology and pathogenesis in anti-CCP-negative RA.

notes.statement: In a genome-wide association study of about 2,000 British rheumatoid arthritis cases and 3,000 shared controls genotyped with the Affymetrix 500K chip, the Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium (2007) found strong associations at the MHC (HLA-DRB1) and at PTPN22. The most associated PTPN22 marker, rs6679677 on 1p13, was perfectly correlated with the functional SNP rs2476601, and its effect size matched previous estimates.
quotes: Both these previous associations emerge strongly here (Table 2). The most associated marker within PTPN22 (rs6679677: chromosome 1p13) is perfectly correlated (HapMap CEU data r2=1) with the functionally relevant SNP (rs2476601) described previously, and the effect size is consistent with previous estimates.

notes.statement: The Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium (2007) found a sex-differentiated association between rheumatoid arthritis and SNP rs11761231 on chromosome 7q32 (P = 3.9 x 10(-7) on the 2-degree-of-freedom sex-differentiated test). The SNP had no effect in males but an additive effect in females (P = 6.8 x 10(-8); odds ratio 1.32). The authors cautioned that the SNP has no correlated neighbors on the chip and that the finding needs further investigation.
quotes: The SNP rs11761231 (chromosome 7) generates a P value of 3.9×10-7 for the 2-degrees of freedom (d.f.) sex-differentiated test which combines trend tests in males and females (Table 3).

This genotype has no effect on disease status in males, but a strong apparently additive effect in females (P value in a logistic regression model with additive log-odds is 0.68 in males and 6.8×10-8 in females, additive OR for females 1.32)

Some caution is therefore required, but this represents a potentially interesting finding which warrants further investigation, particularly given the sex-related prevalence difference characteristic of this condition.

notes.statement: Among SNPs with moderate evidence of association with rheumatoid arthritis (P between 10(-5) and 5 x 10(-7)), the Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium (2007) noted SNPs near the IL2 receptor alpha and beta chain genes: rs2104286 in IL2RA on 10p15 and rs743777 in IL2RB on 22q13. A combined analysis of rheumatoid arthritis and type 1 diabetes cases gave P = 5 x 10(-8) for the IL2RA (CD25) region.
quotes: Of particular interest is the association of SNPs mapping close to both the alpha and beta chains of the IL2 receptor (rs2104286 in the case of IL2RA; rs743777 and IL2RB).
the present study also provides evidence of association with RA (combined trend test P=5×10-8, P=~7×10-6 for RA and T1D separately, Supplementary Table 11)

notes.statement: The Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium (2007) reported that rheumatoid arthritis and type 1 diabetes share susceptibility variants around IL2RA (10p15), PTPN2 (18p11) and the 12q24 region, in addition to the MHC and PTPN22; all three were apparently novel in rheumatoid arthritis. The PTPN2 locus showed a weaker but consistent association with rheumatoid arthritis (P = 1.9 x 10(-2)), with a combined P of 9 x 10(-8) across Crohn disease, type 1 diabetes and rheumatoid arthritis.
quotes: As detailed elsewhere, our study provides data indicating that this list can be extended to include variants around IL2RA (chromosome 10p15), PTPN2 (chromosome 18p11) and the chromosome 12q24 region (Supplementary Table 11), all apparently novel in RA.
The same locus also shows strong association with T1D susceptibility (trend test P=1.9×10-6) and a consistent, though weaker, association with RA (P=1.9×10-2)

notes.statement: The Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium (2007) found only nominal association between rheumatoid arthritis and two CTLA4 SNPs (P = 0.085 and 0.034). Among weaker signals (P 10(-4) to 10(-5)), they noted SNPs in TNFAIP2, GZMB, PRKCQ and KAZALD1; they suggested KAZALD1 might be relevant to bone erosions.
quotes: two SNPs mapping to CTLA-4 (cytotoxic T-lymphocyte associated 4) rs3087243 and rs11571300 were only nominally significant (P=0.085 and P=0.034, respectively)

The association with rs10786617 in KAZALD1 (Kazal-type serine protease inhibitor domain-containing protein 1 precursor), a gene whose product is known to have a role in bone regeneration after injury, may be relevant to the development of bone erosions in RA.

notes.statement: The Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium (2007) noted that susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis is determined by both genetic and environmental factors, with sibling recurrence risk (lambda-s) estimates of 5 to 10. They stated that the known HLA-DRB1 and PTPN22 associations explain around 50% of the familial aggregation.
quotes: Susceptibility to, and severity of, RA are determined by both genetic and environmental factors, with λs estimates ranging from 5-10 (ref.).
These known associations with HLA-DRB1 and PTPN22 explain around 50% of the familial aggregation of RA.

notes.statement: Kallberg et al. (2007) studied interaction between HLA-DRB1 shared epitope (SE) alleles and the PTPN22 R620W allele in 3 case-control studies (Swedish EIRA, North American NARAC, and Dutch Leiden Early Arthritis Clinic), with 1,977 cases and 2,405 controls in total. In all 3 studies they found consistent interaction, defined as departure from additivity, between HLA-DRB1 SE alleles and the A allele of PTPN22 R620W for anti-CCP-positive RA. Multiplicative interaction between the 2 genes was seen only when the 3 studies were pooled.
quotes: in three large case-control studies: the Swedish Epidemiological Investigation of Rheumatoid Arthritis (EIRA) study, the North American RA Consortium (NARAC) study, and the Dutch Leiden Early Arthritis Clinic study (in total, 1,977 cases and 2,405 controls)
Consistent interaction, defined as departure from additivity, between HLA-DRB1 SE alleles and the A allele of PTPN22 R620W was seen in all three studies regarding anti-CCP-positive RA.
Testing for multiplicative interactions demonstrated an interaction between the two genes only when the three studies were pooled.

notes.statement: Kallberg et al. (2007) also used a linkage disequilibrium approach (deviation from independence of penetrance of 2 unlinked loci). This approach indicated interaction between HLA-DRB1 and PTPN22 in the EIRA and NARAC studies and in the pooled analysis.
quotes: The linkage disequilibrium approach indicated a gene-gene interaction in EIRA and NARAC, as well as in the pooled analysis.

notes.statement: In the EIRA study, Kallberg et al. (2007) found no interaction between smoking and PTPN22 R620W. They described a new pattern of interactions between the 2 major genetic risk factors and the major environmental risk factor for anti-CCP-positive RA.
quotes: No interaction was seen between smoking and PTPN22 R620W.
A new pattern of interactions is described between the two major known genetic risk factors and the major environmental risk factor concerning the risk of developing anti-CCP-positive RA.

notes.statement: Kawane et al. (2006) found that Dnase2-/- Ifnar-/- mice and mice with an induced deletion of the Dnase2 gene developed a chronic polyarthritis resembling human rheumatoid arthritis. A set of cytokine genes was strongly activated in the affected joints, and serum contained high levels of anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, rheumatoid factor, and matrix metalloproteinase-3.
quotes: Here we show that DNase II-/-IFN-IR-/- mice and mice with an induced deletion of the DNase II gene develop a chronic polyarthritis resembling human rheumatoid arthritis.

A set of cytokine genes was strongly activated in the affected joints of these mice, and their serum contained high levels of anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, rheumatoid factor and matrix metalloproteinase-3.

notes.statement: Kawane et al. (2006) found that early in disease, Tnfa expression was upregulated in the bone marrow of DNase II-deficient mice, and anti-TNF-alpha antibody prevented arthritis. They concluded that when macrophages cannot degrade mammalian DNA from erythroid precursors and apoptotic cells, they produce TNF-alpha. This activates synovial cells to produce various cytokines, leading to chronic polyarthritis.
quotes: Early in the pathogenesis, expression of the gene encoding tumour necrosis factor (TNF)-alpha was upregulated in the bone marrow, and administration of anti-TNF-alpha antibody prevented the development of arthritis.

These results indicate that if macrophages cannot degrade mammalian DNA from erythroid precursors and apoptotic cells, they produce TNF-alpha, which activates synovial cells to produce various cytokines, leading to the development of chronic polyarthritis.

notes.statement: Rizzo et al. (2006) genotyped the HLA-G 14-bp deletion/insertion polymorphism in healthy individuals and in RA patients treated with methotrexate (MTX). The -14/-14 bp genotype was more common among patients who responded to MTX than among nonresponders (odds ratio 2.46; 95% CI 1.26-4.84; P = 0.009). The authors proposed this polymorphism as a marker of response to therapy in the early phases of the disease.
quotes: The analysis of the HLA-G 14-bp polymorphism in MTX-treated RA patients has confirmed an increase of the -14/-14 bp genotype in the responder group (chi=6.12, P=0.02; chi test) (odds ratio=2.46 (95% confidence interval, 1.26-4.84) P=0.009; logistic regression model).
the association between -14/-14 bp genotype and MTX clinical outcome proposes this polymorphism as a therapy marker in the early phases of the disease.

notes.statement: Rizzo et al. (2006) found that activating peripheral blood mononuclear cells from healthy individuals and from RA patients not treated with MTX with methotrexate induced production of soluble HLA-G (sHLA-G). The highest sHLA-G1 concentrations were significantly associated with the -14/-14 bp genotype. The authors proposed that MTX induces anti-inflammatory sHLA-G molecules that contribute to the therapy response.
quotes: MTX activation induces the production of sHLA-G molecules. A significant association was observed between the highest sHLA-G1 concentrations and the -14/-14 bp genotype.
Our results propose that the MTX induces the production of the anti-inflammatory sHLA-G molecules that concur with the therapy response.

notes.statement: Amos et al. (2006) performed a genomewide linkage scan using more than 5,700 informative SNP markers in 642 Caucasian families with affected sib pairs with RA from the North American Rheumatoid Arthritis Consortium. They found new evidence of linkage at chromosomes 2q33 (lod score 3.52) and 11p12 (lod score 3.09), in addition to a strong, broad linkage interval surrounding the MHC (lod greater than 16).
quotes: The results show striking new evidence of linkage at chromosomes 2q33 and 11p12 with logarithm of odds (LOD) scores of 3.52 and 3.09, respectively.
In addition to a strong and broad linkage interval surrounding the major histocompatibility complex (LOD>16), regions with LOD>2.5 were observed on chromosomes 5 and 10.

notes.statement: Amos et al. (2006) also observed regions with lod scores greater than 2.5 on chromosomes 5 and 10 and additional linkage evidence (lod scores 1.46 to 2.35) on chromosomes 4, 7, 12, 16, and 18. Stratification by anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP) titer status showed significant variation in linkage evidence among strata on chromosomes 4, 5, 6, and 7.
quotes: Additional linkage evidence (LOD scores between 1.46 and 2.35) was also observed on chromosomes 4, 7, 12, 16 and 18.

Stratified analyses according to whether or not the sibling pair members showed elevated anticyclic citrullinated peptide titers indicates significant variation in evidence for linkage among strata on chromosomes 4, 5, 6 and 7.

notes.statement: Amos et al. (2006) attributed the new linkage evidence partly to the higher information content of the Illumina SNP linkage panel (75.6%) compared with a previously used microsatellite panel (mean 52.6%).
quotes: This new evidence for multiple regions of genetic linkage is partly explained by the significantly increased information content of the Illumina IV SNP linkage panel (75.6%) compared with a standard microsatellite linkage panel utilized previously (mean 52.6%).

notes.statement: Seyler et al. (2005) examined 72 rheumatoid synovial tissues representing 3 types of synovitis: ectopic germinal center (GC)-positive, T cell-B cell aggregate, and diffuse. GC+ synovitis had the highest levels of APRIL, which came only from CD83+ dendritic cells. BLyS was present at similar levels in all tissue types and came only from CD68+ macrophages.
quotes: We examined 72 tissues representing the 3 types of synovitis for BLyS and APRIL production and for expression of APRIL/BLyS receptors.
GC+ synovitis had the highest levels of APRIL, produced exclusively by CD83+ DCs. BLyS was present in similar levels in all tissue types and derived exclusively from CD68+ macrophages.

notes.statement: In human synovium-SCID mouse chimeras, Seyler et al. (2005) found that blocking APRIL and BLyS with the decoy receptor TACI:Fc destroyed germinal centers in GC+ synovitis and strongly inhibited IFN-gamma and immunoglobulin transcription. In aggregate and diffuse synovitis, the same treatment left immunoglobulin levels unaffected and increased IFN-gamma production. These different effects correlated with the presence of TACI+ T cells in aggregate and diffuse synovitis and their absence in GC+ synovitis. The authors proposed that BLyS and APRIL have both pro- and antiinflammatory activities in RA.
quotes: In GC+ synovitis, treatment with TACI:Fc resulted in GC destruction and marked inhibition of IFN-gamma and Ig transcription. In contrast, inhibition of APRIL and BLyS in aggregate and diffuse synovitis left Ig levels unaffected and enhanced IFN-gamma production.
These differential immunomodulatory effects correlated with the presence of TACI+ T cells in aggregate and diffuse synovitis and their absence in GC+ synovitis.
We propose that BLyS and APRIL regulate B cell as well as T cell function and have pro- and antiinflammatory activities in RA.

notes.statement: Carlton et al. (2005) sequenced the coding regions of PTPN22 in 48 white North American patients with RA and identified 15 previously unreported SNPs, including 2 coding SNPs in the catalytic domain. They then genotyped 37 SNPs in 475 RA patients and 475 matched controls and replicated selected markers in 661 patients and 1,322 matched controls.
quotes: we sequenced the coding regions of this gene in 48 white North American patients with RA and identified 15 previously unreported SNPs, including 2 coding SNPs in the catalytic domain

We then genotyped 37 SNPs in or near PTPN22 in 475 patients with RA and 475 individually matched controls (sample set 1) and selected a subset of markers for replication in an additional 661 patients with RA and 1,322 individually matched controls (sample set 2).

notes.statement: Carlton et al. (2005) found that the only haplotype carrying the W620 risk allele of PTPN22 (rs2476601) was strongly associated with RA in both sample sets. A haplotype identical at all other SNPs but carrying R620 showed no association.
quotes: The sole haplotype found to carry the previously identified W620 risk allele was strongly associated with disease in both sample sets, whereas another haplotype, identical at all other SNPs but carrying the R620 allele, showed no association.

notes.statement: Carlton et al. (2005) found that R620W did not fully explain the association between PTPN22 and RA. Two SNPs on a single common haplotype were associated with RA independent of R620W, suggesting that at least one additional variant in the PTPN22 region influences RA susceptibility.
quotes: R620W, however, does not fully explain the association between PTPN22 and RA, since significant differences between cases and controls persisted in both sample sets after the haplotype data were stratified by R620W.

Additional analyses identified two SNPs on a single common haplotype that are associated with RA independent of R620W, suggesting that R620W and at least one additional variant in the PTPN22 gene region influence RA susceptibility.

notes.statement: Carlton et al. (2005) predicted 10 common (frequency greater than 1%) PTPN22 haplotypes in white North Americans.
quotes: Analyses of these results predict 10 common (frequency >1%) PTPN22 haplotypes in white North Americans.

notes.statement: Camps et al. (2005) found that Pik3cg -/- mice were largely protected in mouse models of rheumatoid arthritis. The protection correlated with defective neutrophil migration.
quotes: We show that Pik3cg(-/-) mice are largely protected in mouse models of rheumatoid arthritis; this protection correlates with defective neutrophil migration, further validating PI3Kgamma as a therapeutic target.

notes.statement: Camps et al. (2005) developed specific, selective, orally active small-molecule inhibitors of PI3Kgamma. In 2 distinct mouse models of rheumatoid arthritis, oral treatment with one of these inhibitors suppressed the progression of joint inflammation and damage, reproducing the protection seen in Pik3cg -/- mice. The authors suggested that selective PI3Kgamma inhibitors might be useful for treating chronic inflammatory disorders such as rheumatoid arthritis.
quotes: We also describe that oral treatment with a PI3Kgamma inhibitor suppresses the progression of joint inflammation and damage in two distinct mouse models of rheumatoid arthritis, reproducing the protective effects shown by Pik3cg(-/-) mice.
Our results identify selective PI3Kgamma inhibitors as potential therapeutic molecules for the treatment of chronic inflammatory disorders such as rheumatoid arthritis.

notes.statement: Tamiya et al. (2005) performed a whole genome association study of rheumatoid arthritis using 27,039 microsatellites at 100-kb intervals and DNA pooling in 3 successive screens of independent case-control populations, followed by SNP fine mapping. They identified 47 candidate regions; the top 7 loci, which withstood the most stringent statistical tests, were dissected down to individual genes and/or SNPs on 4 chromosomes, including the previously known HLA-DRB1 gene on 6p21.3.
quotes: charting the human genome at 100 kb intervals using a collection of 27,039 microsatellites and the DNA pooling method in three successive genomic screens of independent case-control populations

A total of 47 candidate regions were identified. The top seven loci, withstanding the most stringent statistical tests, were dissected down to individual genes and/or SNPs on four chromosomes, including the previously known 6p21.3-encoded Major Histocompatibility Complex gene, HLA-DRB1.

notes.statement: In a case-control study of white individuals, Begovich et al. (2004) found that the minor allele of a missense SNP in PTPN22, which encodes the hematopoietic-specific protein tyrosine phosphatase Lyp, was associated with RA susceptibility (discovery-study allelic P = 6.6 x 10(-4); replication-study allelic P = 5.6 x 10(-8)).
quotes: Here we report the association of RA susceptibility with the minor allele of a missense SNP in PTPN22 (discovery-study allelic P=6.6 x 10(-4); replication-study allelic P=5.6 x 10(-8)), which encodes a hematopoietic-specific protein tyrosine phosphatase also known as "Lyp."

notes.statement: Begovich et al. (2004) found that the PTPN22 risk allele was present in about 17% of white individuals from the general population and in about 28% of white individuals with RA.
quotes: the risk allele, which is present in approximately 17% of white individuals from the general population and in approximately 28% of white individuals with RA

notes.statement: Begovich et al. (2004) showed that the PTPN22 risk allele disrupts the P1 proline-rich motif important for interaction with Csk, potentially altering the normal function of these proteins as negative regulators of T-cell activation. Because the same allele had been implicated in type 1 diabetes, they suggested that the variant phosphatase may increase overall immune reactivity and heighten a carrier's risk for autoimmune disease.
quotes: disrupts the P1 proline-rich motif that is important for interaction with Csk, potentially altering these proteins' normal function as negative regulators of T-cell activation
suggesting that the variant phosphatase may increase overall reactivity of the immune system and may heighten an individual carrier's risk for autoimmune disease

notes.statement: Begovich et al. (2004) noted that RA is the most common systemic autoimmune disease, affecting about 1% of the adult population worldwide, with an estimated heritability of 60%.
quotes: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is the most common systemic autoimmune disease, affecting approximately 1% of the adult population worldwide, with an estimated heritability of 60%.

notes.statement: John et al. (2004) ran a whole-genome linkage scan with 11,245 SNPs in 157 families with multiple cases of rheumatoid arthritis. The scan detected linkage at HLA-DRB1, the major RA susceptibility locus (P = 0.00004), with a linkage interval of 31 cM. A 10-cM microsatellite scan of the same cohort gave a 50-cM interval.
quotes: Here, we describe a whole-genome screen of 157 families with multiple cases of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), performed using 11,245 genomewide SNPs.
The SNP analysis detected HLA*DRB1, the major RA susceptibility locus (P=.00004), with a linkage interval of 31 cM, compared with a 50-cM linkage interval detected by the microsatellite scan.

notes.statement: John et al. (2004) found 4 more loci at nominal significance (P < 0.05) in the SNP linkage analysis that were not seen in the microsatellite scan. They attributed the differences mainly to the higher information content of the SNPs. When the marker set was reduced to 3,300 SNPs (1-cM spacing), several loci fell below nominal significance.
quotes: In addition, four loci were detected at a nominal significance level (P<.05) in the SNP linkage analysis; these were not observed in the microsatellite scan.

Reducing the number of SNPs in the marker set to 3,300 (1-cM spacing) caused several loci to drop below nominal significance levels, suggesting that decreases in information content can have significant effects on linkage results.

notes.statement: Sakaguchi et al. (2003) found that in mice, a spontaneous point mutation in the gene encoding an SH2 domain of ZAP-70, a key T-cell signal transduction molecule, caused chronic autoimmune arthritis that resembled human RA in many respects.
quotes: Here we show that a spontaneous point mutation of the gene encoding an SH2 domain of ZAP-70, a key signal transduction molecule in T cells, causes chronic autoimmune arthritis in mice that resembles human RA in many aspects.

notes.statement: Sakaguchi et al. (2003) showed that altered signaling from the T-cell antigen receptor through the aberrant ZAP-70 changed the thresholds of T cells to thymic selection. As a result, autoimmune T cells that would otherwise be negatively selected were positively selected. The authors suggested that thymic production of arthritogenic T cells, caused by a genetically determined shift of the T-cell repertoire toward high self-reactivity, might also be crucial to disease development in a subset of patients with RA.
quotes: Altered signal transduction from T-cell antigen receptor through the aberrant ZAP-70 changes the thresholds of T cells to thymic selection, leading to the positive selection of otherwise negatively selected autoimmune T cells.

Thymic production of arthritogenic T cells due to a genetically determined selection shift of the T-cell repertoire towards high self-reactivity might also be crucial to the development of disease in a subset of patients with RA.

notes.statement: Tokuhiro et al. (2003) used SNPs to carry out case-control linkage disequilibrium mapping of the cytokine gene cluster on chromosome 5q31 in the Japanese population.
